source.title: Classicité de formes modulaires surconvergentes
source.authors: Stéphane Bijakowski, Vincent Pilloni and Benoît Stroh
readSections: The published version, freely served by the Annals site, read in full: 40 pages (pp. 975–1014), SHA-256 13c159cde16c09c98de6b29ed1cf0e293ae78e5dc250399a1ee9203b3601d92c, fetched 29 September 2026. Item locators are the journal's pages. Every recorded mistake was checked on a page image. The paper is in French; statements are translated.

summary: Bijakowski, Pilloni and Stroh extend Coleman's classicality criterion from modular curves to PEL Shimura varieties of type (A) and (C) at Iwahori level, with p unramified and totally split in the reflex field: an overconvergent form that is an eigenform of the Hecke operators U_i at the primes of F0 above p, with non-zero eigenvalues and weight large against their valuations, is classical (Theorem 5.3.1). The proof generalises Buzzard–Kassaei: Fargues's degree measures distance from the ordinary-multiplicative tube, the U_i increase it strictly off integer values (so f extends to X_Iw(1−) by finite slope alone), and on the rest U_i^N is decomposed into good and bad parts over good sequences of opens, where Kassaei series converge under the weight–slope hypothesis and glue modulo p^{A_N}. Lan's Köcher principle and rigid GAGA algebraise the result. The PEL moduli, automorphic bundles, Serre–Tate and GAGA are planned; the paper's machinery joins the proposed Part II HigherHidaAndColemanTheory, and its rigid-geometry, degree, PEL linear-algebra and ordinariness, and compactification inputs go to AdicSpacesPartII, HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups T0, PELModuli M0/M2 and ShimuraCompactifications C5. Fourteen mistakes are recorded, including gaps in the dimension ≤ 1 case and in the continuation over half-open boxes.

items.name: PEL data of type (A) and (C)
items.statement: (B, ⋆) a simple Q-algebra with positive involution, centre F ⊇ F0 = F^⋆ totally real of degree d; type (A) when [F : F0] = 2 (B ⊗_{F0,τ} R ≅ M_n(C) with A ↦ Āᵗ), type (C) when F = F0 and B ⊗_{F,τ} R ≅ M_n(R) with A ↦ Aᵗ. With a non-degenerate anti-hermitian B-module (U_Q, ⟨,⟩), G = Aut_B(U_Q, ⟨,⟩) is the group of B-linear symplectic similitudes; G_R ≅ G(∏_τ U(a_τ, b_τ)) in type (A), with a_τ + b_τ = dim_Q U_Q/(2nd) independent of τ, and G_R ≅ G(∏_{i=1}^d Sp_{2a}) in type (C), with a = dim_Q U_Q/(2nd); h : S → G_R, U^{1,0}, the reflex field E. Integral data: an order O_B ⊂ B stable under ⋆ and an O_B-stable lattice U ⊂ U_Q on which ⟨,⟩ is Z-valued.

items.name: Hypothesis 1.1.1: the good prime p
items.statement: p is unramified in F0 and, in type (A), every place of F0 above p splits in F; B ⊗ Q_p is a product of matrix algebras over unramified extensions; O_B is maximal at p; ⟨,⟩ is perfect at p on the lattice U; and p is totally split in E. Then O_B ⊗ Z_p ≅ ∏_{i=1}^h M_n(Z_{p^{d_i}}) ⊕ M_n(Z_{p^{d_i}}) (type (A)) or ∏ M_n(Z_{p^{d_i}}) (type (C)), for the primes π_1, …, π_h of F0 above p with residue degrees d_i.
items.note: M0 owns the PEL data and the linear algebra of O_B ⊗ Z_p; M2 owns the good-prime conditions. The splitting in F of the places of F0 above p (type (A)) and the total splitting of p in E are this paper's additions to M2's conditions.

items.name: Lemma 1.1.4: signatures are constant above each prime of F0
items.statement: Type (A), under Hypothesis 1.1.1. Fix C ≅ C_p and, for each τ : F0 → R, order the embeddings σ, σ̄ of F above τ so that σ lies above π_i^+ (Remark 1.1.3). Then (a_τ, b_τ) = (a_τ′, b_τ′) whenever τ, τ′ lie above the same prime π_i of F0; write (a_i, b_i). (In type (C), a_τ = dim_Q U_Q/(2nd) for every τ.)
items.note: The convention matters: the other choice of σ swaps (a_τ, b_τ) (p. 979). The proof uses Hypothesis 1.1.1(v): det_{U^{1,0}} takes values in Z_p on O_B ⊗ Z_p.

items.name: Morita reduction of O_B ⊗ Z_p-modules
items.statement: M ↦ E_{1,1}·M is an equivalence between the categories of M_n(R)-modules and R-modules, for any ring R (here R = Z_{p^f}).
items.note: Mathlib states exactly this (RingTheory/Morita/Matrix.lean). The paper's next step, that the idempotents F = (F_i^±) identify O_B ⊗ Z_p-modules with modules over ∏ Z_{p^{d_i}} ⊕ Z_{p^{d_i}} (type (A)) or ∏ Z_{p^{d_i}} (type (C)), uses the decomposition of O_B ⊗ Z_p in item 2 and the splitting of modules over a finite product of rings; neither library states it, and it is routine.

items.name: The integral model X without level at p
items.statement: For N ≥ 3 prime to p there is a smooth quasi-projective X over O representing (A, λ, ι, η): A an abelian scheme, λ a prime-to-p polarisation, ι : O_B → End(A) Rosati-compatible with det_{Lie A} = det_{U^{1,0}} (equivalently Lie(A) locally ≅ St ⊗ O_S), and η a symplectic O_B-linear level-N structure lifting étale locally to H_1(A, A_f^p) ≅ U ⊗ A_f^p.
items.note: M2 plans representability and smoothness as an algebraic space; quasi-projectivity is proved at C5 (M2: 'Quasi-projectivity and scheme representability of all these integral algebraic spaces are proved by the compactification step C5').

items.name: Serre–Tate for PEL abelian schemes
items.statement: Over a base on which p is locally nilpotent, deformations of an abelian scheme with O_B-action and polarisation along a nilpotent thickening are equivalent to deformations of its p-divisible group with the induced O_B ⊗ Z_p-action and polarisation.
items.note: The paper uses it as the formal étaleness of P : X → ∏ BT^{d_i}_{a_i+b_i} (§1.3). That form needs the Barsotti–Tate stacks of item 7, which is routed to the Part II downstream of A4, so it is stated there.

items.name: Barsotti–Tate stacks with Iwahori level and the model X_Iw
items.statement: BT^f_m (height mf, Z_{p^f}-action), BT^{f,pol}_l, their formal variants BT̂^f_{l,m} (dimension lf) and BT̂^{f,pol}_l; an Iwahori structure is a full flag 0 = H_0 ⊂ ··· ⊂ H_m = G[p] of Z_{p^f}-stable finite flat subgroups with H_j of rank p^{fj} (in the polarised case up to H_l, totally isotropic); forgetting it is representable and proper; X_Iw := X ×_{∏BT} ∏BT_Iw, proper over X, parametrising (A, λ, ι, η, H_•). By Serre–Tate (item 6) the morphism P : X → ∏_i BT^{d_i}_{a_i+b_i} (type (A); ∏_i BT^{d_i,pol}_{a_i} in type (C)), sending A to ∏ G_i where A[(π_i^+)^∞] = Z^n_{p^{d_i}} ⊗ G_i (resp. A[π_i^∞] = Z^n_{p^{d_i}} ⊗ G_i), is formally étale.

items.name: Automorphic sheaves ω^κ
items.statement: T = Isom_{O_B ⊗ O_X}(St ⊗ O_X, e*Ω^1_{A/X}) is a torsor under M = ∏ Res(GL_{a_i} × GL_{b_i}) (type (A)) or ∏ Res GL_{a_i} (type (C)); for κ ∈ X(T_M)^+, ω^κ = φ_*O_T[κ′] with κ′ = −w_0κ, the functions on (A, λ, ι, η, (ω_i^±)) transforming by κ′ under the Borel B_M.
items.note: B2 constructs the bundle of a Levi representation on the canonical model. The integral sheaf on X and its extension over the compactification (§5.1) belong to C5, as in the accepted extractions of Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni (2021), Calegari–Geraghty (2020) and Pilloni (2020).

items.name: Classical modular forms at Iwahori level
items.statement: Assuming the symmetric space of G has complex dimension > 1 (Hypothesis 1.4.2, so the Köcher principle applies), a modular form of weight κ on X_Iw × Spec K is a global section of ω^κ.

items.name: Fargues's degree of finite flat group schemes
items.statement: For a finite flat group scheme H over O_K̄, deg(H) ∈ [0, log_p |H|] ([Far10]); a morphism H → H′ that is an isomorphism on generic fibres has deg H ≤ deg H′, with equality iff it is an isomorphism ([Far10, coro. 3]); deg G[p] = dim G for a Barsotti–Tate group G; the degree of a truncated Barsotti–Tate group of level one is an integer ([Pil11, lem. 2.1]); and deg is additive in short exact sequences of finite flat group schemes over O_K̄ (used on p. 992 for deg(H_l) = fl − deg(L)).
items.locator: §1.5, p. 987; proofs of Propositions 3.1.1–3.1.2, pp. 992–993 (published version)

items.name: The degree map δ and the ordinary-multiplicative locus
items.statement: δ(G, H_•) = deg(H_l) ∈ [0, fl]. For G of dimension fl (G from BT̂^f_{l,m}, or BT̂^{f,pol}_l with m = 2l), (G, H_•) is ordinary-multiplicative when δ = fl; then G is an extension of an étale BT of height f(m − l) by a multiplicative one and H_l is multiplicative. On the Raynaud generic fibre X^rig_Iw this gives δ : X^rig_Iw → ∏ [0, d_ia_i] (the i-th coordinate with f = d_i, l = a_i) and the opens X_Iw(ε) = {δ_i ≥ d_ia_i − ε_i}; X_Iw(0) is the ordinary-multiplicative tube. The degree is analytic: on the moduli of subgroups there are sections δ_L of invertible sheaves with |δ_L(x)| = p^{−deg L(x)} ([Pil11, §2.2.2], p. 1000), so for rational a ≤ b the set δ_i^{−1}([a, b]) is a quasi-compact open, and on C_i^rig the function δ_i∘p_2 − δ_i∘p_1 is the valuation of an analytic function (p. 993).

items.name: Wedhorn's ordinariness theorem
items.statement: p is totally split in E if and only if the ordinary locus is dense in X × Spec(O/π) ([Wed99, 1.6.3]).
items.note: The Iwahori-level consequences in Remark 1.5.1 need the model X_Iw of item 7 and are item 43, in the Part II.

items.name: Overconvergent modular forms
items.statement: M(X_Iw, κ)† = colim_{ε > 0} H^0(X_Iw(ε), ω^κ), the Q_p-space of overconvergent forms of weight κ.
items.note: OverconvergentAutomorphicForms O3 and O8 define overconvergent spaces for Hilbert and Siegel varieties as colimits over neighbourhoods of the ordinary locus, but not for PEL types (A) and (C) at Iwahori level, and O8 makes no classicality claim; the design should reuse that formalism.

items.name: Hecke correspondences on Barsotti–Tate stacks
items.statement: Over Spec(K): C^BT parametrises (G, H_•, L) with G of height mf with Z_{p^f}-action (resp. principally polarised of height 2lf), H_• an Iwahori structure and L ⊂ G[p] Z_{p^f}-stable (L Lagrangian in the polarised case) with L ⊕ H_l = G[p]; p_1 forgets L and p_2 sends it to (G/L, H′_•) with H′_k the image of H_k for k ≤ l and of p^{−1}(H_k ∩ L) for l < k ≤ m (non-polarised case); p_1, p_2 : C^BT → BT^f_{m,Iw} × Spec(K) (resp. BT^{f,pol}_{l,Iw} × Spec(K)) are representable, finite and étale. Taking schematic closures over O_K̄ gives U : P(BT_Iw(O_K̄)) → P(BT_Iw(O_K̄)), which sends finite sets to finite sets.

items.name: Hecke correspondences C_i on X_Iw and the operators U_i on opens
items.statement: For 1 ≤ i ≤ h, C_i := (X_Iw × Spec K) ×_{BT_Iw × Spec K} C^BT (via p_1, equivalently via p_2, Remark 2.2.1) parametrises O_B-stable L ⊂ A[π_i] of type U_i, and p_1, p_2 : C_i → X_Iw × Spec(K) are finite étale. A/L gets the polarisation x_i·λ for a chosen totally positive x_i ∈ O_{F0} with v_{π_j}(x_i) = δ_{ij} (p·λ when there is one place above p), so U_i is canonical only up to this choice. With C_i^rig := X^rig_Iw ×_{X^an_Iw} C_i^an, U_i(V) = p_2(p_1^{−1}(V)) on admissible opens V of X^rig_Iw.

items.name: The Hecke operators U_i on modular forms
items.statement: Ũ_i = Tr_{p_1} ∘ (π_i^*)^{−1} ∘ p_2^* and U_i = p^{−n_i}Ũ_i with n_i = d_ia_ib_i (type (A)) or d_ia_i(a_i + 1)/2 (type (C)); explicitly U_i(f)(A, …) = p^{−n_i} Σ_{L of type U_i} f(A/L, …); they act on classical and overconvergent forms and commute.
items.note: OverconvergentAutomorphicForms O6 plans the p-level correspondences at the primes above p for Hilbert varieties only.

items.name: Propositions 3.1.1–3.1.3: U does not decrease the degree
items.statement: For x ∈ BT̂^f_{l,m,Iw}(O_K̄) and y ∈ U({x}), δ(y) ≥ δ(x); if equality holds for some y then H_l is a truncated BT of level one and G[p] = H_l ⊕ (another Z_{p^f}-stable truncated BT_1), so δ(x) is an integer; likewise in the polarised case, with both summands totally isotropic.

items.name: Proposition 3.2.1 and Corollary 3.2.2: dynamics of U_i
items.statement: For integers 0 ≤ n_i ≤ d_ia_i − 1 and reals 0 < η_i ≤ ν_i < 1 there is N with U_i^N(δ_i^{−1}[d_ia_i − n_i − ν_i, d_ia_i]) ⊂ δ_i^{−1}[d_ia_i − n_i − η_i, d_ia_i]; the U_i commute and U_i preserves δ_j for j ≠ i, so (∏ U_i)^N(X_Iw(n + ν)) ⊂ X_Iw(n + η).

items.name: Proposition 4.1.2 (Kassaei, Bartenwerfer): bounded sections
items.statement: For a locally free F on an admissible formal scheme with smooth reduced generic fibre and V ⊆ Z^rig quasi-compact, H^0(V, F^rig) ≅ K ⊗_O lim_n H^0(V, F̃^rig/p^n), where F̃^rig is the subsheaf of sections of norm ≤ 1 ([Kas06, lem. 2.3], [Pil11, coro. 5.1]). The norm is the canonical Banach norm on H^0(V, F^rig) ([Kas06, §2]); a cohomological correspondence T : H^0(T(V), F^rig) → H^0(V, F^rig) has operator norm |T|_V (§4.1.1), which Lemma 4.4.5 bounds.

items.name: Propositions 4.1.4, 4.1.6, 4.1.7: finite étale maps and strict neighbourhoods
items.statement: A finite étale map of rigid spaces sends opens (quasi-compact opens) to opens (quasi-compact opens) ([Bos09]); strict neighbourhoods are stable under finite intersections and unions; and a finite étale f between quasi-compact rigid spaces sends a strict neighbourhood of U to a strict neighbourhood of f(U) (via [BL93, lem. 5.7, th. 5.2, coro. 5.3] and [AM04, lem. A.1.1]).

items.name: Proposition 4.1.8: a finiteness criterion
items.statement: For f : X → Y finite étale between separated rigid spaces and an open U ⊆ X with U → X quasi-compact, if the geometric fibres of f|_U have constant cardinality then f|_U and f|_{X∖U} are finite étale.

items.name: Identity principle for rigid analytic sections
items.statement: A section of a locally free sheaf on a connected (smooth) rigid space is determined by its restriction to a non-empty open ([Ber96, prop. 0.1.13]); so an extension of an overconvergent form, when it exists, is unique.

items.name: Proposition 4.2.1: continuation to X_Iw(1−)
items.statement: If f ∈ M(X_Iw, κ)† is an eigenform of each U_i with eigenvalue α_i ≠ 0, then f extends canonically to X_Iw(1−) = {δ_i > d_ia_i − 1 for all i}, for every weight κ (only finite slope is used).

items.name: Good sequences of opens and the count N(x, β)
items.statement: A good sequence of a quasi-compact open V is a decreasing sequence (V_k) of quasi-compact opens with V_0 = V and V_k = ∅ for k ≫ 0. On U_γ = δ^{−1}(I_1 × ··· × [0, d_ia_i − 1 + γ] × ··· × I_h), N(x, β) counts y ∈ U_i({x}) with δ_i(y) ≤ d_ia_i − 1 + β, equivalently complements L_0 of type U_i with deg L_0 ≥ n(1 − β) (Remark 4.3.4), and U_k = {N(x, β) ≥ k} is a good sequence of U_γ (Lemma 4.3.6).

items.name: Proposition 4.3.7 and Remark 4.3.8: splitting U_i into good and bad parts
items.statement: On U_k ∖ U_{k+1}, N(x, β) = k and U_i = U_i^good ⊔ U_i^bad as finite étale correspondences, U_i^bad being the k complements of degree ≥ n(1 − β); U_i^good lands in δ_i^{−1}(]d_ia_i − 1 + β, d_ia_i]) and U_i^bad in δ_i^{−1}([0, d_ia_i − 1 + β]).

items.name: Proposition 4.3.10: overconvergence of the good sequence
items.statement: For β < β′ < ε and U′_k = {N(x, β′) ≥ k}, U′_k is a strict neighbourhood of U_k for every k ≥ 1.

items.name: Theorem 4.4.1: decomposition of U_i^N
items.statement: For N ≥ 1 and γ, β < ε there are a finite totally ordered S_N and a good sequence (U_k(N))_{k ∈ S_N} of U_γ, of length independent of γ, such that on each U_k(N) ∖ U_{k+1}(N), U_i^N = (⊔_{j<N} U_i^{N−1−j} ∘ T_j) ⊔ T_N with T_j = U^good ∘ (bad)^j, the good operators landing in δ_i^{−1}(]d_ia_i − 1 + β, d_ia_i]) and the bad ones in δ_i^{−1}([0, d_ia_i − 1 + β]); the sequences can be overconverged (β′ > β gives strict neighbourhoods).
items.locator: Theorem 4.4.1, pp. 1000–1001; proof and Lemmas 4.4.2–4.4.4, pp. 1001–1004 (published version)

items.name: Lemma 4.4.5: norm of the bad operators
items.statement: If U_i^bad on V involves only complements L_0 of type U_i with deg L ≥ ν, where L = F_i^+·L_0 in type (A) and L = F_i·L_0 in type (C) (so deg L_0 = n·deg L, Remark 4.3.4), then ‖U_i^bad‖_V ≤ p^{d_ia_ib_i − ν·inf_j(k_{i,j,a_i} + l_{i,j,b_i})} (type (A)) or p^{d_ia_i(a_i+1)/2 − ν·inf_j k_{i,j,a_i}} (type (C)), κ written as (k_{i,j,1} ≥ ··· ; l_{i,j,1} ≥ ···).

items.name: Hypothesis 4.5.1: the weight–slope condition
items.statement: Write κ = ∏_{i=1}^h ∏_{j=1}^{d_i}(k_{i,j,1} ≥ ⋯ ≥ k_{i,j,a_i}; l_{i,j,1} ≥ ⋯ ≥ l_{i,j,b_i}) in type (A) and ∏_{i,j}(k_{i,j,1} ≥ ⋯ ≥ k_{i,j,a_i}) in type (C) (p. 994), so that k_{i,j,a_i} and l_{i,j,b_i} are the smallest entries. For every 1 ≤ i ≤ h, inf_j(k_{i,j,a_i} + l_{i,j,b_i}) > v(α_i) + d_ia_ib_i in type (A), and inf_j k_{i,j,a_i} > v(α_i) + d_ia_i(a_i + 1)/2 in type (C).

items.name: Definition 4.5.2 and Lemma 4.5.3: Kassaei series
items.statement: On V′_k ∖ V_{k+1}, f_{N,k} = α_i^{−1}U^good_{i,k}f + Σ_{j=1}^{N−1} Σ α_i^{−j−1}U^bad ··· U^bad U^good f; with u_0 = p^{n_i + v(α_i) − (1−ε)·inf(weights)} < 1 (Hypothesis 4.5.1), the f_{N,k} are bounded by |α_i^{−1}|p^{n_i}M uniformly in N and k.

items.name: Lemma 4.5.5: Kassaei series agree up to u_0^N
Propositions 4.5.6–4.5.7: gluing the Kassaei series
items.statement: The f_{N,k} glue to g_N ∈ H^0(U, ω̃^κ/p^{A_N}) with A_N → ∞; the g_N form a projective system, so they define g ∈ H^0(U, ω^κ) (by Proposition 4.1.2), which agrees with f on W.

items.name: Proposition 4.5.8: continuation to the whole rigid space
items.statement: Under Hypothesis 4.5.1 the eigenform f extends to an element of H^0(X^rig_Iw, ω^κ), one direction i at a time. The proof applies §4.5 on boxes with half-open sides, where §4.5 needs closed ones; the exhaustion step is missing (E12).

items.name: Toroidal compactifications at Iwahori level (Lan)
items.statement: For a projective polyhedral cone decomposition S of X_Iw × K ([Lan15, déf. 2.7, prop. 2.8]) there is a projective X^S_Iw over O whose generic fibre is the toroidal compactification of X_Iw × K ([Lan15, §3]). It is built as a compactification of the normalization X^n_Iw of an auxiliary Siegel model in X_Iw × K ([Lan16, Example 13.12]; printed 'rem. 13.12', E14), and it contains X^n_Iw as a dense open. The forgetful map extends to X^S_Iw → X^S ([Lan13, th. 6.4.1.1], [Lan15, prop. 7.3]), and ω^κ extends to a locally free sheaf, formally canonical modulo every power of π ([Lan, coro. 5.8–5.9]). That the moduli model X_Iw is X^n_Iw is item 35.

items.name: Normality of the Iwahori-level model
items.statement: The moduli model X_Iw is normal, by [He13] or by [Str10, prop. 3.1.7.1] together with the flatness of local models ([Gör01] in type (A), [Gör03] in type (C)). Hence X_Iw is the normalization model X^n_Iw of item 34 and a dense open of X^S_Iw ([Lan16, rem. 16.5]).
items.note: M4 plans normality only for the normalization model ('Do not assert smoothness, a fine moduli interpretation, or a universal abelian scheme on such a normalization without a separate theorem'). The moduli model is item 7, and its normality rests on PEL local models (Görtz, He), which no layer plans; the accepted extractions of Pilloni (2020) and Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni (2021) also keep Iwahori local-model geometry in their Part IIs.

items.name: Proposition 5.2.1: Köcher principle modulo π^n (Lan)
items.statement: If the symmetric space of G has complex dimension > 1, restriction H^0(X̄^S_Iw × Spec(O/π^n), ω^κ) → H^0(X^n_Iw × Spec(O/π^n), ω^κ) is an isomorphism for all n ≥ 1 and κ ∈ X^+(T_M) ([Lan15, th. 8.7]), X^n_Iw being the normalization model of item 34. With item 35 the target is H^0(X_Iw × Spec(O/π^n), ω^κ), which is Proposition 5.2.1.

items.name: Corollaries 5.2.2–5.2.3: formal and rigid Köcher principles
items.statement: Passing to the limit over n, H^0(𝔛̄^S_Iw, ω^κ) ≅ H^0(𝔛_Iw, ω^κ) for the π-adic formal completions (Corollary 5.2.2), and on rigid generic fibres H^0((𝔛̄^S_Iw)^rig, ω^κ) ≅ H^0(X^rig_Iw, ω^κ) (Corollary 5.2.3).

items.name: Rigid GAGA (Kiehl)
items.statement: Analytification gives H^0(X̄^S_Iw × Spec K, ω^κ) ≅ H^0((X̄^S_Iw)^rig, ω^κ) ([Kie67]).

items.name: Coleman's classicality theorem on modular curves (Coleman, Kassaei)
items.statement: An overconvergent eigenform of weight k on a modular curve of Iwahori level at p, with U_p-eigenvalue α such that k > 1 + v(α), is classical ([Col96]; Kassaei's proof [Kas06] via Buzzard's dynamics [Buz03]).
items.locator: Introduction, pp. 975–976; proof of Theorem 5.3.1, p. 1011 (published version)
items.note: PadicFamilies L2 plans the analogous small-slope classicality for the eigencurve built from modular symbols, not Coleman's theorem for overconvergent forms.

items.name: Theorem 5.3.1: classicality of overconvergent forms of small slope
items.statement: Let X_Iw be a PEL Shimura variety of type (A) or (C) of Iwahori level at p satisfying Hypothesis 1.1.1, κ ∈ X^+(T_M) and f ∈ M(X_Iw, κ)† an eigenform of every U_i (1 ≤ i ≤ h) with non-zero eigenvalue α_i. If κ and the v(α_i) satisfy Hypothesis 4.5.1, f is classical, i.e. in the image of H^0(X_Iw × Spec K, ω^κ) ↪ M(X_Iw, κ)†. (When Hypothesis 1.4.2 fails the paper's argument needs completing, see E6; so does the continuation over half-open boxes, see E12.)

items.name: Explicit weight–slope conditions
items.statement: For the Siegel variety of GSp_{2g} over a totally real F of degree d with p inert, the condition is inf_σ k_{σ,g} > v(α) + dg(g + 1)/2; for a unitary group of signature (a, b) over a CM field F with p inert in F0 and split in F, it is inf_σ(k_{σ,a} + l_{σ,b}) > v(α) + dab.
items.locator: Remark after the main theorem, p. 977 (published version)

items.name: Maximum modulus principle for rigid spaces
items.statement: On a quasi-compact rigid space the absolute value of an analytic function attains its maximum, so its valuation attains its minimum. With item 11 this makes the increase of δ_i under U_i uniform on quasi-compact opens (proof of Proposition 3.2.1).

items.name: Remark 1.5.1: ordinary loci at Iwahori level
items.statement: Under Hypothesis 1.1.1 the ordinary and the ordinary-multiplicative loci of X_Iw × Spec(O/π) are non-empty, so X_Iw(0) ≠ ∅ (from item 12). The ordinary locus is dense in X_Iw × Spec(O/π) if p is totally split in F and, for p unramified in F, only then. The paper asserts this ('On peut montrer'), pointing only to an enumeration of the codimension-zero Kottwitz–Rapoport strata.

routes.reason: R0 constructs finite and étale maps of rigid spaces, R2 owns admissible formal schemes, blow-ups and generic fibres, and R3 coherent sheaves, finite étale traces and Kiehl-type finiteness. The paper's general rigid-geometry inputs are statements about those objects, used by any analytic-continuation argument: the Kassaei–Bartenwerfer description of sections by bounded sections, images of opens and strict neighbourhoods under finite étale maps (through Bosch–Lütkebohmert flattening), the finiteness criterion 4.1.8, the identity principle and the maximum modulus principle. PAPER-PILLONI-20's accepted route sends Bartenwerfer's theorems to R0, R2 and R3 as well.

T0 holds Fargues's degree. The accepted routes of PAPER-BOXER-PILLONI-26 (route 12) and PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-PILLONI-21 (route 13) send the degree, its divisor and the comparison for generic isomorphisms ([Far10, coro. 3]) there, and T0 builds on the Barsotti–Tate API of FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.1–R07.2 without defining a second one. This item coalesces with theirs; a route to R07.1 would give the degree a second owner.

M0 owns PEL data, their real signatures and the reflex field, and M2 the smooth PEL model at a good prime. Lemma 1.1.4 (signatures constant above each prime of F0 under Hypothesis 1.1.1) is linear algebra of that data, and Wedhorn's theorem, that the ordinary locus of the special fibre of X is dense exactly when p splits completely in the reflex field, is a statement about M2's model. The Iwahori-level clauses of Remark 1.5.1 need the model X_Iw of item 7 and stay with the Part II (item 43).

C5 owns integral PEL compactifications, including 'higher p-level normalizations'. Lan's toroidal compactification of the Iwahori-level normalization model, the extension of the automorphic sheaves and Lan's Köcher principle modulo π^n are results of that layer. Items 34 and 36 are stated for the normalization model, which M4 and C5 own; its identification with the moduli model X_Iw of item 7 is item 35, in the Part II. Stated for X_Iw itself they would need item 7, which is downstream of C5.

routes.title: Hida and Coleman families, period modules, and family L-functions, Part II: higher Hida and higher Coleman theory for coherent cohomology
routes.brief: This route joins the proposal of HigherHidaAndColemanTheory made from PAPER-PILLONI-20 and joined by PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-PILLONI-21 and PAPER-BOXER-PILLONI-26 (same id, parent, title and area); the design job merges its brief with theirs. Bijakowski–Pilloni–Stroh (Ann. of Math. 183 (2016), 975–1014) supply the degree-0 Coleman theory for PEL Shimura varieties of type (A) and (C) at Iwahori level with p unramified and split in the reflex field: Theorem 5.3.1, an overconvergent eigenform of every U_i with non-zero eigenvalues and weight large against the slopes (Hypothesis 4.5.1: for every 1 ≤ i ≤ h, inf_{1≤j≤d_i}(k_{i,j,a_i} + l_{i,j,b_i}) > v(α_i) + d_ia_ib_i in type (A) and inf_{1≤j≤d_i} k_{i,j,a_i} > v(α_i) + d_ia_i(a_i + 1)/2 in type (C), k_{i,j,a_i} and l_{i,j,b_i} being the smallest entries of κ) is classical. Build, in order: Barsotti–Tate stacks with Iwahori level and X_Iw, with its normality, which identifies it with ShimuraCompactifications C5's normalization model, and its ordinary loci (Remark 1.5.1); Fargues's degree map δ and the ordinary-multiplicative tube; overconvergent forms; the Hecke correspondences U_i normalised by p^{−n_i}; the dynamics (Propositions 3.1.1–3.2.2); continuation to X_Iw(1−) by finite slope alone; the good/bad decomposition of U_i^N over good sequences of opens (§§4.3–4.4) with the norm bound of Lemma 4.4.5; Kassaei series and their gluing modulo p^{A_N} (§4.5), on closed boxes and then exhausting the half-open ones (PAPER-BIJAKOWSKI-PILLONI-STROH-16/E12); and the formal and rigid Köcher principles with GAGA to algebraise. Keep the case where the symmetric space has dimension ≤ 1 explicit (PAPER-BIJAKOWSKI-PILLONI-STROH-16/E6): Coleman–Kassaei covers only the modular curve. Import PEL moduli (PELModuli M0, M2, M4), Serre–Tate (AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A4), automorphic bundles and classical forms (AutomorphicBundles B2, B4), Fargues's degree (HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups T0), rigid geometry and GAGA (AdicSpacesPartII R0–R3), Lemma 1.1.4 and Wedhorn's theorem (PELModuli M0, M2) and Lan's compactifications of the normalization model and Köcher principle (ShimuraCompactifications C5). The higher Coleman theory of the joined briefs recovers this degree-0 statement for GSp_{2g}; the design should record the comparison rather than build two classicality theorems for the same group.
routes.reason: Classicality of small-slope overconvergent forms is Coleman theory for coherent cohomology in degree 0, which is exactly the direction of the proposed HigherHidaAndColemanTheory; PadicFamilies itself stops at modular curves and totally real fields in one degree, and OverconvergentAutomorphicForms builds coefficient sheaves, not classicality.

sourceIssues.locator: Proof of Theorem 5.3.1, p. 1011, and Remark 5.3.2 (published version)
sourceIssues.printed: The source claims that failure of Hypothesis 1.4.2 for G makes its symmetric space the Poincaré half-plane, and that [Col96] or [Kas06] then proves the theorem.
sourceIssues.correction: When the symmetric space has dimension ≤ 1 the variety need not be a modular curve: type (C) with B an indefinite quaternion algebra over Q (n = 2) gives Shimura curves, type (A) with Σ_τ a_τb_τ = 1 gives unitary curves, and Σ a_τb_τ = 0 gives finite sets. For compact curves, and for the zero-dimensional cases (where the symmetric space is a point, not the Poincaré half-plane), X_Iw is proper, and the continuation of §4 (which does not use Hypothesis 1.4.2) together with GAGA on X_Iw proves the theorem; non-compact unitary curves need the cusp analysis of Remark 5.3.2 or a comparison with modular curves.
sourceIssues.reason: [Col96] and [Kas06] treat the modular curve (GL_2 over Q). Theorem 5.3.1 assumes only Hypothesis 1.1.1, which allows those other PEL data, and Definition 1.4.3 relies on Hypothesis 1.4.2 to ignore cusps.

review.reason: Checked on the p. 1011 image and against §1.1. Type (C) needs only F = F0 and B ⊗_{F,τ} R ≅ M_n(R) with the transpose involution (p. 979), so an indefinite quaternion division algebra over Q with p ∤ disc(B) satisfies Hypothesis 1.1.1 and gives compact Shimura curves. Type (A) with d = 2 and signatures (1, 1) and (0, 2) above the two primes of F0 over a split p is allowed by Lemma 1.1.4 and gives compact unitary curves; definite signatures give zero-dimensional varieties, where 'donc a le demi-plan de Poincaré' is itself false. [Col96] and [Kas06] treat only modular curves, and [Joh13], cited in the introduction, gives for quaternionic curves over Q only the classicality of the Hecke eigenvalues (Theorem 33(b)), so it does not close the gap. The repair holds, and the correction is amended to cover the zero-dimensional cases, which are proper too. Gap, affects the proof.

sourceIssues.printed: The source assumes the symmetric space of G has complex dimension > 1, then recasts this, using §1.1 notation, as d > 1 or a_1 > 1 if d = 1.
sourceIssues.correction: The dimension is Σ_τ a_τb_τ in type (A) and d·a(a + 1)/2 in type (C); the reformulation is right in type (C) only.
sourceIssues.reason: In type (A), U(1, 2) over an imaginary quadratic field (d = 1, a_1 = 1) has a 2-dimensional symmetric space, and d = 2 with signatures (1, 1) and (0, 2) (p split in F0) gives dimension 1 although d > 1. Proposition 5.2.1 uses the dimension condition itself (Lan's theorem), so nothing downstream depends on the reformulation.

In the proof of Proposition 4.5.8, extend f over each box whose sides are [d_ja_j − 1 + η, d_ja_j] for j > i, for every rational η > 0, and glue: at each point both extensions are limits of the Kassaei series computed from f on the U_i^N-images of that point, so they agree on overlaps, and these boxes form an admissible covering of the box with half-open sides, since each δ_j is −log_p of the absolute value of a section (item 11).
sourceIssues.reason: With I_j = ]d_ja_j − 1, d_ja_j] for some j, as in every step of the proof of Proposition 4.5.8 but the last, δ_i^{−1}([d_ia_i − 1 + β_0, d_ia_i]) ∩ W_0 is the increasing union of the quasi-compact opens where δ_j ≥ d_ja_j − 1 + η, and is not quasi-compact. So f, known only on W, need not be bounded there, and M need not exist. Likewise U_γ is then not quasi-compact, which Definition 4.3.2 (good sequences of a quasi-compact open) and Proposition 4.1.2 need. The repair is routine, but the paper does not state it.
